relationships.subject: IL-17A
relationships.evidence_quote: The results consistently demonstrated an elevated HMGB1 expression alongside pyroptosis-related proteins, providing strong evidence that IL-17A triggers pyroptosis, leading to the release of dsHMGB1 in PECs

relationships.subject: Bz-ATP
relationships.evidence_quote: Bz-ATP reversed the protective effect of the anti-IL-17A antibody on prostate epithelial cell pyroptosis

relationships.subject: dsHMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: Flow cytometry analysis revealed a significantly greater proportion of M1 macrophage in the dsHMGB1 group than this in the control group

relationships.subject: dsHMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: The protein levels of p-Jak2, p-Stat1, and Pfkp were markedly increased in the dsHMGB1 group when compared to the control group

relationships.subject: Stat1
relationships.evidence_quote: luciferase and ChIP-qPCR assays provided further evidence that Stat1 functions as a transcriptional activator of Pfkp

relationships.subject: Pfkp
relationships.evidence_quote: Pfkp served as a crucial rate-limiting enzyme in regulating glycolysis

relationships.subject: fludarabine
relationships.evidence_quote: Flow cytometry analysis revealed that fludarabine significant inhibited dsHMGB1-induced M1 macrophage polarization

relationships.subject: glycyrrhizic acid
relationships.evidence_quote: These findings suggest that GA can alleviate prostate tissue inflammation and inhibit M1 macrophage polarization in EAP mice.

key_findings: IL-17A-induced pyroptosis of prostate epithelial cells releases dsHMGB1, which drives M1 macrophage polarization via Jak2/Stat1-dependent Pfkp transcription and glycolysis in EAP
Glycyrrhizic acid (HMGB1 inhibitor) and fludarabine (Stat1 inhibitor) reduced inflammation and M1 polarization
